query: For as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys in the form of nanoscale thin films or lithographically patterned nanoribbons, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles, given that the notable response reported for bulk forms may not persist in a genuinely low-dimensional state and that heat-transfer rate limits cycle frequency? Specify one controlled intervention, predicted observations relative to the as-deposited baseline, applicable operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In nanoscale, as-deposited Fe–Mn–Ni–Ge–Si high-entropy alloy (HEA) films, the magnitude of the magnetocaloric entropy change (ΔS) and the size of thermal/magnetic hysteresis during low-field cycling are primarily governed by the ability of a first-order martensitic-like magneto-structural transition to proceed cooperatively. Substrate-induced biaxial compressive strain and < ~40 nm columnar grains frustrate the lattice distortion that accompanies the transition, suppressing ΔS and enlarging hysteresis. Brief vacuum rapid-thermal annealing (RTA) at ≃500 °C allows partial relaxation of epitaxial/thermal stresses and coarsens grains beyond a critical ≃50 nm diameter, restoring cooperative atomic shuffles and reducing interfacial energy barriers, thereby (1) approximately doubling ΔS under a 0–1 T field change and (2) cutting thermal hysteresis by one-third compared with the as-deposited state.
generation.material_initial_state: Magnetron-sputtered, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi HEA thin film (or 500-nm-wide nanoribbons) on oxidised Si substrate; thickness 50–200 nm; columnar grains ≲40 nm; high residual compressive stress (~500 MPa); no post-deposition heat treatment.
generation.intervention: Vacuum rapid-thermal annealing at 500 ± 10 °C for 120 s followed by Ar quench to room temperature (heating/cooling >100 °C s⁻¹).
generation.conditions: Magnetic-cooling cycles with field µ₀H = 0→1 T at sweep rate ≤0.1 T s⁻¹; temperature window 200–350 K; cycling frequency ≤1 Hz to avoid external heat-transfer limits; measurements performed with film firmly attached to substrate (no freestanding state).
generation.structural_mediator: Average in-plane residual strain and grain size distribution (sub-critical <40 nm vs post-anneal >50 nm).
generation.mechanism: Substrate clamping and fine grains pin the martensitic lattice distortion, broadening/ suppressing the first-order magneto-structural transition that generates the magnetocaloric effect. RTA relieves biaxial strain and enables grain growth, lowering the elastic and interfacial energy barriers so that the transformation proceeds more completely and reversibly in low magnetic fields.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the as-deposited baseline: (a) peak |ΔS| increases from ~1 ± 0.2 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ~2 ± 0.3 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for µ₀ΔH = 1 T; (b) thermal hysteresis width decreases from ~20 ± 2 K to ~13–15 K; (c) adiabatic temperature change |ΔT_ad| rises proportionally (~0.6 K → ~1.2 K).
generation.baseline: As-deposited films: suppressed/ broadened transition; |ΔS| ≃1 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, hysteresis ≃20 K, ΔT_ad ≃0.6 K under 0–1 T field change at 300 K.
generation.boundary: Film thickness 50–200 nm; grain size after anneal ≤100 nm (to avoid strain relaxation via cracking); anneal temperature window 450–550 °C (above: interdiffusion with SiO₂ or elemental segregation degrades MCE); field changes ≤1 T; cycling frequencies ≤1 Hz (limited by interfacial thermal resistance).
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: quantitative gains may vary with exact composition, substrate thermal expansion mismatch, and oxygen uptake during RTA; complete recovery of bulk-like ΔS (>4 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) is not expected.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare identical HEA film/nanoribbon sets; keep one as-deposited (control) and subject the other to the specified RTA. Measure (i) temperature-dependent magnetisation M(T,H) during 0–1 T field sweeps and (ii) differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) under identical heating/cooling rates to extract ΔS and hysteresis widths.
measurements: Isothermal M(H) curves every 2 K around transition
X-ray diffraction peak positions/widths for strain and grain size
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If post-anneal samples do NOT display (1) ≥50 % increase in peak |ΔS| AND (2) ≥25 % decrease in hysteresis width compared with the as-deposited control under identical 0–1 T cycling, the hypothesis is falsified.
